ecological_model.name: source_pool_handoff
ecological_model.statement: The effective source context of island occurrence shifts from mainland-anchored isolation toward archipelago-internal occupied source continuity as mainland access becomes extreme.
ecological_model.mainland_source_rich_prediction: after climate, island area, mainland isolation and source proximity are supplied, species-conditioned topology is weak or redundant
ecological_model.remote_prediction: within a response-independent extreme-isolation tail, units retaining occupied insular source-network continuity have more occurrence support than equally remote units lacking that continuity
ecological_model.mechanistic_interpretation: source-network continuity may reflect colonization access, rescue/persistence or historical occupancy connectivity; the primary occurrence analysis does not distinguish these mechanisms

primary_prediction.name: extreme_isolation_topology_regime_switch
primary_prediction.extreme_isolation_rule: upper 25% of the frozen eligible-unit isolation distribution computed from predictor-only data before response access
primary_prediction.contrast: mean candidate-minus-reference held-out loss in extreme-isolation units minus mean candidate-minus-reference held-out loss in non-extreme units
primary_prediction.statement: After a strong ecological reference is supplied, the incremental held-out effect of a species-conditioned structural coordinate is more favourable in the upper 25% of a response-independent isolation distribution than in the remaining eligible units.

remote_but_linked_vs_remote_unlinked.prediction: candidate-minus-reference loss is more favourable in remote-but-linked than remote-and-unlinked units

multihop_continuity.definition: connected to a permitted occupied source at the smallest frozen graph scale while nearest permitted occupied source distance exceeds that scale
multihop_continuity.prediction: multi-hop source-network state retains occurrence information after nearest-source distance is represented

source_saturation.moderator: response-blind source/range breadth defined before confirmatory response access
source_saturation.prediction: topology is most redundant for broad-source species in mainland-source-rich settings, with redundancy attenuated in extreme-isolation settings

independent_biological_discrimination.contemporary_colonization: requires repeated occupancy/transition data and predeclared 0_to_1 analysis
independent_biological_discrimination.rescue_or_persistence: requires repeated occupancy and separately predeclared 1_to_0 or 1_to_1 analysis

cross_system_generalization.minimum_requirement: same-direction primary regime-switch result in at least one independently admitted island system under spatial transfer
cross_system_generalization.stronger_requirement: replication across independently admitted island archipelagos with distinct geography and source pools
cross_system_generalization.fragmentation_analogy: habitat fragments may test an analogous source-network handoff but are not treated as the same biogeographic process as true islands

anti_selection: do not select a new system because its known outcome supports source-pool handoff
do not change the 0.75 extreme-isolation threshold after response access
do not choose generic connectivity or smallest graph scale after seeing response outcomes
do not select taxa by favourable A-Islands subgroup behaviour
do not count A-Islands exploratory statistics as confirmation
do not infer realized stepping-stone movement from graph paths
